In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PPC has a dual function in visuomotor control.
the PPC is not only involved in spatial target selection but also plays a role in nonspatial effec-tor selection.
the posterior parieto-frontal network is involved in both the selection and the preparation of the motor plans for the execution of the selected action.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spatial target selection is more integrated than nonspatial effektor decisions.
spatial and nonspatial decisions are processed in a different manner in the posterior parieteal cortex.
the PPC is not a single, homogenous region but rather consists of a mosaic of functionally distinct areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PPC contains multiple representations of motor plans that may be used in the service of different types of decisions.
the same decisional process may be represented differently by distinct cortical areas, and that these different representations may be used to implement distinct decisional strategies.
the brain is not a serial processor of information, but rather it is a highly parallel system that can perform many computations at once.
